chapter: Bird, the band's breakup and Luis Russell
title: Bird fired for the fight with Walter Brown and then rehired
summary: After Bird and Brown's slow-motion fight, Ben Bart demanded he be fired; Ramey became his agent and got him back.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: : Well, when -- now, there's -- I'm a little confused about when Bird leaves McShann.

Well now, there's -- we played the Savoy, as you know, and then we went into the Apollo and played that. And we went back into the Savoy, and we had an incident there on a Sunday afternoon. Bird had gone over to Walter Brown's wife. Her name was Jean something -- Jean Brown -- and she -- and had gotten Walter Brown's last $5.00 from his wife.
And so Brown -- Bird was on the bandstand. Brown was, standing in front of the bandstand ready to get on, and Brown come in and asked him where is his -- why did he come

and talk his wife out of the last $5.00 he had, you know. And so they got in a fight. And no blows was thrown, but they were trying to hit each other, and they were so high. Each was so high, they never made contact, and it was a picture of a slow motion fight like we've seen.
They were swinging at each other?
Swinging at each other and never -- they would swing and fall down.
But somehow this man that actually had the booking charge of our band, his name was Ben Bart out of Glaser's office --

MR. RAMEY: Yeah. And he came up and he said, he gave us a lecture, you know, and we got to rehearsal, and he stopped us, and he came, and he says, you know, for every musician on this bandstand, we got musicians here in New York can blow rings around them. So no man is that important to this unit that they're going to ruin this thing. So as of this day I'm demanding Max Shann fire Charlie Parker immediately. So Max Shann let him go. Now, we were on our way back into the Apollo again. We had really upset them the first time, you know, him playing and Walter Brown singing with the band. (Inaudible).

And so they got Jimmy Cole in the band. Well, after about two weeks we started getting so many complaints and things, and Bird would come by, and different ones of us would give him some money to eat and so forth. He was still working at the Monroe's Uptown House, you know, after hour joint, but he didn't make no money.

And so I got McShann to let me -- let me hire Bird and he pay me -- you know, I'd act as Bird's agent. And I'd take care of him, you know. So we got Bird back in the band. And I think Cole stayed with us then. He did and started playing baritone.
